cards.front: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients with fewer than 4 cycles a year need induced [___] (with combined oral contraceptive pill or cyclic progestogen) to prevent endometrial hyperplasia.
cards.context:
In PCOS the persistent anovulation means unopposed estrogen drives continuous endometrial proliferation without the cyclic progesterone-driven shedding that protects the lining in normal cycles.

The fix is to recreate the missing progesterone signal. COCP delivers cyclic progestogen plus contraception (ideal in young women planning pregnancy later).

cards.front: The first newborn assessment checks tone, breathing and [___].
cards.context:
The first check is tone, breathing and heart rate. Good tone means the limbs are moving and the posture is flexed.

A baby who is very floppy and not moving is much more likely to need active resuscitation. Colour is not part of that first check.

cards.front: A woman with pre-eclampsia at or after 37 weeks is treated definitively, without delay, by [___].
cards.context: At or after 37 weeks, the fetal benefit of further time is minimal. Maternal risk of eclampsia, HELLP, abruption or stroke makes prompt delivery the right call (HYPITAT).

cards.front: A newborn has microcephaly and confirmed sensorineural hearing loss. Cranial imaging shows calcifications concentrated around the ventricles. The congenital infection most strongly suggested by this pattern is [___].
cards.context:
Periventricular calcification together with microcephaly and hearing loss favours congenital cytomegalovirus.

Toxoplasmosis can also calcify the brain, but its typical scattered pattern, hydrocephalus and chorioretinitis form a different clinical cluster.

cards.front: The flexion point for vacuum-cup placement lies about 3 cm anterior to the [___] fontanelle.
cards.context: Centring the cup over the flexion point promotes head flexion. This landmark must be identified during assessment; the short delivery clip cannot confirm the original application.

cards.front: Normal pregnancy arterial blood gas (ABG) shows a chronic compensated [___] alkalosis with PaCO₂ around 30 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ around 18-22 mmol/L.
cards.context: The driver is progesterone, which acts on the central respiratory chemoreceptors to raise tidal volume by ~40% (rate is unchanged). The kidneys then excrete bicarbonate to keep pH near the upper limit of normal.

cards.front: The commonest cause of postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), about 70% of cases, is uterine [___].
cards.context:
The 4 T's are a bedside search ordered by frequency, so you work the likeliest cause first.

Tone (~70%, boggy uterus → massage + uterotonics), Trauma (~20%, inspect for tears/haematoma), Tissue (~10%, check placenta is complete → manual removal), Thrombin (~1%, coagulopathy → blood products).

Run all four — atony is commonest but a contracted uterus that keeps bleeding means you have missed trauma or a coagulation problem.

cards.front: Normal cardiotocograph (CTG): baseline 110-160 bpm, variability [___] bpm, accelerations present, no decelerations.
cards.context:
Normal CTG has four reassuring features: baseline 110-160 bpm (bradycardia <110 may be cord/heart block, tachycardia >160 may be sepsis/hypoxia).

DR C BRAVADO structures interpretation: Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline Rate, Variability, Accelerations, Decelerations, Overall.

cards.front: A pregnant woman taking benzodiazepines should not stop them abruptly, because abrupt withdrawal can cause maternal [___].
cards.context:
Abrupt opioid cessation in pregnancy precipitates withdrawal in mother and fetus, risking fetal distress and preterm labour. Abrupt benzo cessation risks maternal seizures.

Frame as non-judgemental harm reduction — women who feel judged stop attending antenatal care.

cards.front: The first-line treatment for significant neonatal unconjugated jaundice is [___].
cards.context: Phototherapy converts unconjugated bilirubin in the skin to water-soluble isomers the baby can excrete. It's plotted against age-specific thresholds; exchange transfusion is reserved for dangerously high levels.

cards.front: With the hip flexed and abducted, lifting the greater trochanter forward to reduce a dislocated hip is the [___] manoeuvre.
cards.context:
Ortolani (pull anteriorly) tests if a DISLOCATED hip can be reduced: flex, abduct, lift the greater trochanter forward; a clunk means the head has reduced.

Mnemonic: Barlow Backward, Ortolani Out. Both become unreliable after 3 months.

cards.front: Empirical antibiotics for early-onset neonatal sepsis: benzylpenicillin (covers GBS) + [___] (covers Gram-negatives like E. coli); stop at 36-48 hours if cultures negative + well.
cards.context:
EONS (<72 h) is dominated by vertically transmitted maternal flora — GBS and E. coli account for ~70%.

Empirical antibiotics target both: benzylpenicillin (GBS, Listeria, syphilis) + gentamicin (E. coli and other Gram-negatives, synergistic with penicillin against GBS); doses benzylpen 60 mg/kg IV 12-hourly.

LONS (>72 h) more often nosocomial — flucloxacillin (Staph) + gent. Add aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 8-hourly if HSV suspected (vesicles, focal neurology, maternal active genital herpes).

cards.front: Small for gestational age (SGA) = estimated fetal weight (EFW) <10th centile; fetal growth restriction (FGR) is pathological, usually below the 3rd centile or abnormal [___].
cards.context:
The trap: SGA is a size label, FGR is a diagnosis of failed growth potential.

SGA just means EFW <10th centile. Many are constitutionally small but healthy (small parents, female fetus), needing only surveillance to confirm normal velocity with normal Dopplers.

FGR means the fetus has not reached its growth potential: EFW or abdominal circumference <3rd centile, absent end-diastolic flow, or <10th with abnormal Dopplers or falling centiles. It can occur above the 10th.

cards.front: Recurrent miscarriage is now defined as [___] or more pregnancy losses before 20 weeks.
cards.context:
Recurrent miscarriage is two or more confirmed intrauterine losses before 20 weeks; older definitions required three. Important actionable causes include antiphospholipid syndrome and uterine anomalies.

Test for anticardiolipin, lupus anticoagulant and anti-β2GP1; positivity must persist at least 12 weeks apart to confirm APS.

Analyse pregnancy tissue when available. Consider parental karyotyping case by case, including when tissue analysis is unavailable.

reference.title: Miscarriage, Recurrent Miscarriage and Ectopic Pregnancy (C-Gyn 38)

cards.front: With continued postpartum bleeding at 500 mL or more, medical escalation should occur before waiting for [___].
cards.context: NSW GL2025_013: continued bleeding at ≥500 mL requires immediate medical escalation even before observations become abnormal. Normal early blood pressure can reflect compensation, not absence of serious bleeding.

cards.front: Tranexamic acid should be given within [___] of birth for PPH at a dose of 1 g IV (WOMAN trial evidence).
cards.context:
The WOMAN trial (2017) demonstrated that IV tranexamic acid 1g given within 3 hours of birth reduces death from bleeding in women with PPH, with no increase in thromboembolic events.

It should be given early — benefit decreases with each hour of delay. WHO recommends TXA within 3 hours for all women with PPH.

cards.front: A woman in active labour has a cephalic fetus, normal growth and liquor, normal uterine activity, and no risk factors. The appropriate fetal monitoring method is [___].
cards.context:
Queensland guidance recommends intermittent auscultation for active labour when there are no antenatal or intrapartum risk factors and the clinical picture is reassuring.

Continuous cardiotocography becomes appropriate when risk or fetal findings change.

cards.front: During maternal cardiac arrest from 20 weeks, aortocaval compression is relieved by [___] so she can stay supine for chest compressions.
cards.context:
The gravid uterus compresses the large vessels when she lies flat, so venous return and cardiac output fall. Shifting the uterus to the left relieves that compression.

A full lateral roll does the same job for the vessels but spoils chest compressions. Displacement keeps her supine enough for effective CPR.

cards.front: Initial intrauterine resuscitation for prolonged fetal bradycardia: maternal repositioning and stop [___]; if persistent, proceed to category 1 caesarean.
cards.context:
Prolonged fetal bradycardia (FHR <110 for >3 min) is a peripartum emergency. If unresolved by 9 min or with an abnormal CTG, proceed to category 1 caesarean.

Caesarean urgency (RANZCOG): Cat 1 = immediate threat to mother/fetus, deliver ≤30 min; Cat 2 = compromise without immediate threat, ≤75 min; Cat 3 = early delivery, no compromise; Cat 4 = elective.

cards.front: Elevated middle cerebral artery (MCA) peak systolic velocity (>1.5 multiples of the median) suggests fetal anaemia; treatment may require intrauterine [___].
cards.context:
Fetal anaemia drops blood viscosity, which paradoxically RAISES peak systolic velocity in the MCA — the brain compensates for reduced O₂ carriage by increasing flow.

When PSV crosses threshold, refer urgently to MFM for IUT via cordocentesis.

cards.front: A newborn becomes jaundiced at 12 hours, with anaemia, reticulocytosis and predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia. This pattern suggests [___].
cards.context:
Early jaundice with anaemia and reticulocytosis suggests increased bilirubin production from red-cell breakdown.

Assess for immune and non-immune causes; the pattern alone does not identify a specific cause.

cards.front: After the fetal head delivers, it untwists slightly to realign with the shoulders — this movement is called [___].
cards.context:
Restitution is the small reverse rotation of the delivered head, realigning it with the shoulders' position in the pelvis.

It precedes the larger external rotation that accompanies shoulder engagement with the AP diameter.

cards.front: The first mechanical step in managing postpartum haemorrhage from atony is uterine [___].
cards.context:
Most PPH is uterine atony, so the first mechanical step is fundal massage to rub up a contraction, alongside uterotonics (oxytocin first).

If bleeding continues, bimanual compression (a fist in the anterior fornix against a hand on the fundus) slows it while theatre is prepared.

cards.front: A term baby whose mother takes stable methadone becomes tremulous, difficult to settle and feeds poorly at 48 hours. The cry is high-pitched. Assessment finds no infection or metabolic disturbance. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
Delayed irritability and feeding dysfunction fit withdrawal after placental opioid exposure ends. Stable maternal treatment does not eliminate neonatal risk.

Central nervous system irritability and gastrointestinal dysfunction explain the symptom cluster. Infection and metabolic disorders can mimic or coexist with withdrawal.

cards.front: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first [___] and continued breastfeeding with complementary foods until at least 2 years.
cards.context:
The benefit is dose-dependent: longer exclusive breastfeeding means lower infant mortality, fewer episodes of gastroenteritis and otitis media, less atopy and obesity, and better cognitive outcomes.

Mothers gain reduced breast and ovarian cancer risk.

Australian uptake falls off fast — ~60% exclusive at discharge but only ~25% by 6 months, driven by return-to-work pressure, formula marketing, and unsupported lactation.
